sources.entry: Snipe-IT | IT asset and license management

summary.one_liner: Snipe-IT is a free, open-source, web-based IT asset management system for tracking who has which equipment, purchase data for depreciation, and software licenses.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Snipe-IT as a FOSS project for asset management in IT operations, covering things like knowing who has which laptop, when it was purchased for depreciation, and handling software licenses. It is built on Laravel 12 and runs on a web server, accessed through a browser rather than as a desktop executable. The README says it runs on Mac OS X, Linux, and Windows, and that a Docker image is available. It exposes a JSON REST API, and the README notes several third-party libraries and modules (such as Python, PowerShell, Perl, and .NET wrappers, and sync scripts for JAMF, Kandji, Mosyle, and UniFi) that build on it. Detailed installation, user manual, upgrading, and translation documentation are linked from the README rather than included in it.
use_cases: track which employee has which laptop
sync asset inventory with MDM tools
how_to_run: Follow the installation manual linked from the README to install and configure Snipe-IT on a web server
Review the requirements documentation for full system requirements
Alternatively, use the Docker image mentioned in the README
notable: Built on Laravel 12 and actively developed with frequent releases
Provides a JSON REST API that many third-party integrations use
Third-party ecosystem includes JAMF, Kandji, Mosyle, UniFi, Jira, and Kubernetes Helm chart integrations
Mobile apps from third parties for iOS and Android
caveats: Web-based only; must be hosted on a web server and accessed via a browser
Third-party libraries and modules are not supported by the Snipe-IT maintainers and come with no reliability guarantees
Security vulnerabilities should be reported by email rather than the public issue tracker
